articleTitle: Olap and ELK Exploration of Large Data Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: By exploiting various tools for processing massive data, data extraction is an essential means of ensuring the reliability and quality of a BI information system. However, decision making has led us to exploit the technical differences of data mining. Thus, the data warehouse models information with the aim of improving results when processing this data instantaneously. This article presents a method for improving the efficiency of big data mining using the ELK stack and OLAP methodology. This approach enables users to analyze data quickly and efficiently.

articleTitle: Research on Bitcoin Inscriptions Risk Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the proposal of Bitcoin ordinal theory, Bitcoin inscriptions have gradually become an industry hotspot, which promotes the development of Bitcoin ecology, but also brings the risk of digital content on the Bitcoin chain. For example, inscriptions containing politically sensitive or pornographic information are fully uploaded and permanently stored on the chain in a tamper-proof manner, so Bitcoin inscriptions are more risky than Ether NFTs. In this paper, we propose a bitcoin inscription parsing method, which parses the inscriptions from the original bitcoin transactions, solidifies evidence of wallet addresses associated with risky inscriptions, extracts all the inscriptions inscribed by the associated wallet addresses with the information of the on-chain transactions, and realizes the on-chain risk monitoring of bitcoin inscriptions. Meanwhile, this paper implements a risk monitoring system for Bitcoin inscriptions and associated addresses. The experimental results show that the bitcoin inscription parsing method proposed in this paper can effectively parse out all the on-chain inscriptions of bitcoin, and the risk monitoring system can effectively monitor risky bitcoin inscriptions and their associated addresses.

articleTitle: A Location Usability Measure Method for Distribute K-Anonymity Privacy Protection in LBS
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Distributed K-anonymity is a well-known method for protecting location privacy in location-based services. In this method, the request user constructs an anonymous cloaking region with the real locations of cooperative users and then submits this region to location-based service provider (LSP). However, when directly adopting the existing schemes, the malicious cooperative users do not share their real locations with the request user but instead provide fake locations. If the request user employs these fake locations to construct the anonymous cloaking region, LSP can effectively reduce the anonymous cloaking region or even directly identify the real location of the request user. Therefore, the existing distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> -anonymity schemes cannot completely protect the request user's location privacy. To solve this problem, based on the historical location dataset, this paper filters out the fake locations that can be identified by taking into account three aspects, namely visited time, visited distance, and visited frequency. In this way, the constructed anonymous cloaking region can be used to protect the request user's location privacy successfully. Extensive experiments indicate that the proposal is effective and efficient.

articleTitle: Homomorphic Encryption-Based Privacy Protection Data Processing Strategies in Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), real-time processing and privacy protection for traffic data become particularly important. In this research, we explore how to process traffic data efficiently and securely in fog computing environments, especially in wireless in-vehicle networks. First, we propose a homomorphic encryption-based strategy that performs computation on ciphertexts, eliminating the need for frequent decryption and thus achieving higher data processing efficiency. Then, we provide an in-depth discussion on data integrity and real-time performance, and propose a novel data validation method to ensure data integrity and real-time updates in fog computing environments. In addition, we designed a series of simulation experiments using virtual data to verify the effectiveness of our approach. The experimental results show that our strategy not only greatly improves the data processing speed, but also effectively guarantees the privacy and integrity of the data. Overall, this study provides a new and efficient method for traffic data processing in fog computing environments, which is an important reference value for future traffic data processing.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Trusted Traceability in Agarwood Supply Chain Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: The agarwood industry in Hainan possesses significant economic value, and strengthening the management of the agarwood supply chain is of great significance. Currently, the detection standards for agarwood products cannot ascertain relevant information such as the origin, and there is no systematic traceability method. Moreover, traditional traceability methods carry the risk of information tampering. In response, we propose a trustworthy traceability scheme for the agarwood industry. It establishes an optimized model for agarwood supply chain traceability storage based on blockchain technology. This model utilizes a multi-chain architecture to facilitate rapid query of transaction information and employs smart contracts to achieve supply chain information traceability. Our approach not only enables traceability of information in the agarwood supply chain but also enhances query efficiency compared to traditional single-chain structures.

articleTitle: Interpretable MOOC Course Recommendations Based on Reinforcement Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the large amount of educational information on online education platforms causing information overload, it is particularly important to select personalized content suitable for users from a large number of courses. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning method using MOOC knowledge graph as the environment to generate explainable recommended course paths, recommend courses to users and give clear explanations, so that students can understand the reasons and logic of the recommendations. The MOOC knowledge graph covers a variety of complex relationships and learners' historical records, while reinforcement learning simulates the interaction between users and courses to make recommendation decisions. Experiments were conducted on the MOOC data set, and the experimental results proved that the method combining knowledge graph and reinforcement learning proposed in this article improved the NDCG and HR indicators.

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation Index System of Postgraduate Deep Learning Based on AHP
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: As an important part of educational and teaching activities, the construction of an evaluation index system for deep learning is particularly important for guiding and promoting graduate students' deep learning. This article mainly uses the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to construct a deep learning evaluation index system. AHPResearch on the evaluation index system of postgraduate deep learning shows that the evaluation index system of postgraduate deep learning includes four primary indicators and sixteen secondary indicators. Among them, the two primary indicators of thinking structure and motor skills, and the two secondary indicators of expansion structure and association structure have the greatest impact on postgraduate deep learning.

articleTitle: Research on Low-Cost Deployment and Low Energy Consumption Auxiliary Communication Methods Based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Considering the limited communication of ground IoT devices in wide-area agricultural reclamation areas, this paper proposes a method of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collaborative coverage to minimize the number of UAVs and UAV's energy consumption while meeting the needs of regional signal coverage. Firstly, with the goal of maximizing coverage area, the optimization of UAV cooperative coverage strategy is achieved under constraints such as UAV multi machine interference, UAV energy constraints, and node received signal-to-noise ratio. Through simulation experiments, the impact of UAV flight speed on communication energy consumption in different distance scenarios is analyzed, and energy consumption optimization is achieved in the scenario of maximizing UAV coverage area. Therefore, the multi machine collaborative coverage methods proposed in this article can meet the needs of UAV assisted enhanced communication coverage scenarios, and to some extent, improve the coverage quality of weak signal areas.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Access Control Model for E-Medical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the high speed development of information technology, the healthcare system increasingly relies on cloud servers for data storage and complex computation, patient data privacy issues stem from healthcare systems' vulnerability to breaches, despite data encryption emphasis, insufficient focus on preventing unauthorized access risks compromises patient information confidentiality. Consequently, the need to protect privacy within the healthcare system has gained significant attentions. However, existing research primarily concentrates on data encryption processes, but there is comparatively less attention given to addressing potential privacy leaks concerning data visitors. In this paper, we propose a privacy-preserving access control model for healthcare cloud data visitors. Our model combines the RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) model with the PSI (Private Set Intersection) technique to ensure the privacy and security of data visitors. The performance analysis of our proposed solution demonstrates its relative efficiency and practicality when applied to E-medical systems.

articleTitle: Application of Hierarchical Attention Network in Vulnerability Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Machine learning methods have found extensive use within the realm of code vulnerability detection. Enhancing the effective integration of machine learning techniques into code vulnerability detection has emerged as a crucial avenue of research. The outcomes of vulnerability detection are primarily influenced by the extraction hierarchy of source code semantic information and the preprocessing of code in earlier stages. However, many current technological studies remain at levels above the source code and lack a systematic preprocessing approach, which is insufficient for detecting code vulnerability patterns. We propose a vulnerability detection solution based on Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing for source code data processing and the utilization of a Hierarchical Attention Network (HAN) to construct the model. Our approach reduces a significant amount of redundant data, saving substantial computational expenses, while also enhancing model interpretability. Our experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms other cases listed in the article in terms of vulnerability prediction efficiency and interpretability of vulnerability weights.

articleTitle: Intellectual Property Data Trading Through NFTization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Intellectual Property (IP) is a special type of data that has broad and high trading demands. Existing blockchain-based IP data trading schemes can promote the IP data trading market by removing the dependence on centralized platforms. However, the problem of trading fairness among sellers and buyers is more challenging compared to centralized approaches. This paper addresses the trading fairness problem by representing the data as Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) and separating usage rights and ownership. An NFTized IP data trading system is designed and a two-stage fair trading scheme is proposed. They ensure that buyers need not pay additional money if the IP content is not useful for them, and the sellers will not lose the IP ownership until they receive additional money in the second stage of trading. A prototype for the system is realized, and based on it, a set of experiments are carried out to evaluate the performance. The experimental results show the cost is acceptable.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing Application of Multi-Sensor Earth Observation Images as the Big Data: A KOMPSAT Use Case
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: In the era of big data, the importance of Earth Observation (EO) satellite imagery is increasing. However, satellite imagery cannot be directly used without pre-processing and calibration. Recently, products called Analysis Ready Data (ARD) have been developed that complete these pre-processing tasks and allow users to use satellite information immediately. This study aims to explain the concept and components of cloud computing-based Soft-as-a-Service (SaaS) that provide numerical functions to generate ARD. We also present a case study in which satellite imagery derivative products generated by this SaaS by open source stack are fused with other types of satellite imagery, such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), to create high-value products such as soil moisture for agriculture applications or environmental studies. In this study, we used Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite (KOMPSAT)-3/3A optical imagery and KOMPSAT-5 SAR satellite imagery. As the demand for satellite imagery increases worldwide, the need for such fusion research is expected to increase as many application areas that process it as big data are generated.

articleTitle: MOOC Session-Based Recommendation Algorithm of Multi-Interests
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: To provide users with more accurate course recommendations, some current massive open online course (MOOC) platforms adopt session-based recommendation methods. However, existing session-based recommendation methods fail to address situations where user interests are complex. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes the MOOC session-based recommendation algorithm of multi-interest (MSRAMI). In the recommended session flow, MSRAMI incorporates multiple options to consider users' diverse interests. Additionally, during the neural network embedding process, a multi-head attention mechanism is employed to integrate all interests into the decision space. When compared to existing MOOC recommendation methods, the proposed approach demonstrates improvements in HR and NDCG metrics.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Responsible Gaming Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Responsible gaming aims at maintaining the integrity and sustainability of the gaming industry. However, The exchange of sensitive data, such as player and gaming related information, among different parties raises significant privacy concerns, and safeguarding privacy becomes a top priority consideration throughout the design and implementation of responsible gaming systems. In this paper, we introduce an innovative scheme that utilizes Oblivious Transfer (OT) and Private Set Intersection (PSI) protocols to address privacy concerns of responsible gaming systems. Our scheme proposes a system model that addresses privacy concerns related to player global limits and banned player list query and response, without requiring infrastructure changes, unlike blockchain-based solutions; Our proposed scheme not only addresses privacy concerns between the query user and the centralized database server but also mitigates privacy concerns between the query user and certificate authority (CA) by incorporating blind RSA signature scheme; Our proposed scheme achieves linear complexity in computation and communication, while remaining resilient against malicious adversaries under the random oracle model.

articleTitle: Research on Re-Identification of Amur Tigers and Bengal Tigers
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: This study was devoted to the individual identification of different tiger subspecies, a relatively little covered research area. As one of the endangered species in the world, the tiger's population monitoring and conservation is critical. However, traditional tiger monitoring methods face numerous challenges, including difficulties in identification, inconvenient data access and high costs. In this study, we adopted a machine recognition approach using the EfficientNetB6 deep learning model as the base model and combined it with a transfer learning strategy for the purpose of recognizing individuals of different tiger subspecies. We constructed a large-scale image database containing two subspecies of tigers and labelled it in detail. Through transfer learning, we successfully applied the EfficientNetB6 model for the tiger individual recognition task, overcoming the difficulties of data scarcity and differences between subspecies. The experimental results showed that the training set accuracy of the EfficientNetB6 model was 98.0%, while the validation set accuracy was 93.0%. This study provides a novel and efficient method in the field of wildlife conservation, which is expected to improve tiger monitoring and population management. In addition, our method also offers valuable references and methodologies for individual recognition studies of other large mammals.

articleTitle: Differentially Private Spatiotemporal Trajectory Synthesis with Retained Data Utility
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Spatiotemporal trajectories collected from GPS-enabled devices are of vital importance to many applications, such as urban planning and traffic analysis. Due to the privacy leakage concerns, many privacy-preserving trajectory publishing methods have been proposed. However, most of them could not strike a good balance between privacy protection and good data utility. In this paper, we propose DP-STTS, a differentially private spatiotemporal trajectory synthesizer with high data utility, which employs a model composed of a start spatiotemporal cube distribution and a 1-order Markov process. Specially, DP-STTS firstly discretizes the raw spatiotemporal trajectories into neighboring cubes, such that the model size is limited and the model's tolerance for noise could be enhanced. Then, a Markov process is utilized for the next location point picking. After adding noise under differential privacy (DP) to the model, synthetic traj ectories that preserve essential spatial and temporal characteristics of the real trajectories are generated from the noisy model. Experiments on one real-life dataset demonstrate that DP-STTS provides good data utility. Our code is available at https://github.com/Etherious72/DP-STTS.

articleTitle: A Citation Count Prediction Model Based on Bi-LSTM and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the accelerated growth of the count of academic papers, the establishment of an effective prediction model to evaluate the academic impact of potential papers has become a hot topic of academic attention, aiming at helping scholars quickly identify high-quality papers and inspire them with the most popular research topics. With the extensive deployment of deep learning, as well as in the field of citation prediction, it has been verified that the metadata text of academic papers has a tremendous impact on the count of citations. In this work, a deep learning model based on Bi-LSTM and Transformer is proposed to further improve the performance of such citationcount prediction model in the field of artificial intelligence, owing to the dedicated engagement of the metadata text from abstract, early 5-years citations and cross-attention mechanisms. The experimental results show that the proposed model can outperform the most recent baselines, indicating its great advantages in the field of citation prediction.

articleTitle: Rumor Spreading and User Behavioral Characteristics Based on Social Network Analysis and Co-Word Network Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the development of the Internet and social media, many problems and challenges have arisen, among which the negative impact of rumors on society needs to be urgently addressed. Weibo, as a representative social media platform in China, has a large number of users. Therefore, studying rumor propagation and user behavior characteristics on the Weibo can help reduce the harm of rumors on society. In this paper, social network analysis is used to study the impact of different classes of users (bystanders, debunkers, and rumor mongers) on rumor propagation on Weibo. This result show that rumor debunkers play an important role in suppressing rumor propagation, and specific phrases such as “really” and “credibility” play a key role in suppressing rumor propagation. By analyzing the behavioral characteristics of different users involved in rumor spreading, this paper aims to improve the reference suggestions for related platforms, to reduce the harm caused by rumor spreading.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Tongue Image Segmentation Research
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the development of modern medical imaging and artificial intelligence, tongue image segmentation has become a critical step in intelligent tongue diagnosis systems. The quality of segmentation directly impacts subsequent diagnoses, necessitating precise tongue segmentation to reduce interference from irrelevant regions and enhance diagnostic accuracy. Currently, both traditional tongue image segmentation methods and certain deep learning approaches have yet to attain the required levels of accuracy and speed for effective tongue image segmentation. In this paper, we conducted research based on deep learning, using the UNet model for medical image segmentation as a foundation. We combined Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Transformers equipped with attention mechanisms. Additionally, we introduced the novel neural network operator called Involution. As a result of these efforts, we achieved a remarkable 99.05 percent accuracy in segmenting tongue images, primarily collected by Prof. Zhao's team. We applied this segmentation method to the tongue diagnostic process for conditions such as Qi deficiency and tongue pain. When applied to the tongue diagnosis process in the tongue image classification of Qi deficiency and calm quality tongue images, the classification effect is improved by about 10 percent compared with the classification effect without tongue image segmentation. When applied to the tongue image classification for Qi deficiency and calm quality tongue tongue images in the tongue diagnostic process,our method improved the classification accuracy by approximately 10 percent compared to classification without tongue image segmentation.

articleTitle: Peer-to-Peer International Trade Model Based on Blockchain and Smart Contracts: Theory and Practice of BTLC
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: This study focuses on BTLC, a peer-to-peer international trade model based on blockchain and smart contracts, which aims to reform the traditional let- ter of credit process, improve international trade efficiency, reduce costs and improve security. By elaborating the BTLC model, this study demonstrates how blockchain technology as well as smart contract technology can be applied in the field of international trade to effectively solve the problems existing in the tra- ditional letter of credit process, such as high transaction costs due to too many intermediaries, high transaction risks due to an imperfect trust mechanism, and inefficiency in transactions. In addition, this paper further proves the superiority of the BTLC model in theory and practice through empirical research. It provides an in-depth discussion of the potential application and development direction of the model in future research. However, there are still some challenges and lim- itations in the practical application of the BTLC model. These challenges and limitations include the need for further empirical studies to validate the model's effectiveness and the problems faced. These include technical standards, laws and regulations. Therefore, this study suggests that future research directions should focus on the implementation challenges of blockchain technology, as well as the application of blockchain technology in other fields, in order to promote the wide application of blockchain technology in international trade.

articleTitle: Regularization Mixup Adversarial Training: A Defense Strategy for Membership Privacy with Model Availability Assurance
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Neural network models face two highly destructive threats in real-world applications: membership inference attacks (MIAs) and adversarial attacks (AAs). One compromises the model's confidentiality, leading to membership privacy breaches, while the other disrupts the model's availability, rendering it dysfunctional. Recent work has shown that adversarial examples can pose dual threats to neural network models, both MIAs and AAs, so that these two different types of attacks have a certain degree of intersection. However, existing defense methods typically focus on defending against one of the two attacks and cannot simultaneously address both. To address the above issues, we propose a defense method called regularization mixup adversarial training (RMAT), aiming to protect model membership privacy while ensuring model availability. The core idea of RMAT is to use a continuous augmentation strategy during training to generate mixup adversarial examples, weakening attackers' understanding of membership data, and updating the model with a new membership-weighted loss strategy to improve its generalization ability for handling unknown samples. This approach can further protect the model's membership privacy and ensure model availability. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to single defense strategies, RMAT can simultaneously protect the model's membership privacy and availability.

articleTitle: Key Management and Authentication Scheme Forward Trusted Pervasive Container Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Cloud computing technology is an internet-based computing model that provides high reliability and security measures, including data backup, secure access control, etc. As Docker containers play a increasingly important role in traditional cloud computing architectures, the communication needs between containers become prominent. However, existing container to container communication mainly relies on network protocols for file transfer, making it difficult to achieve the expected results in cloud cluster security. Therefore, this paper primarily focuses on container based keys and proposes a container identity trusted key management method based on Pervasive container computing architecture. The experimental results demonstrate that the container identity trusted key management method not only meets the security transmission characteristics required in the container cloud architecture, but also adopts a strategy combined with trusted hardware, providing security guarantees. In addition, the method proposed in this article that combines trusted hardware for signature verification can defend against multiple network attacks compared to traditional container architectures without using security policies.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Bandwidth Nightmare: CDN Compression Format Conversion Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) are designed to enhance network performance and protect against web attack traffic for their hosting websites. And the HTTP compression request mechanism primarily aims to reduce unnecessary network transfers. However, we find that the specification failed to consider the security risks introduced when CDNs meet compression requests. In this paper, we present a novel HTTP amplification attack, CDN Compression Format Convert(CDN-Convet) Attacks. It allows attackers to massively exhaust not only the outgoing bandwidth of the origin servers deployed behind CDNs but also the bandwidth of CDN surrogate nodes. We examined the CDN-Convet attacks on 11 popular CDNs to evaluate the feasibility and real-world impacts. Our experimental results show that all these CDNs are affected by the CDN-Convet attacks. We have also disclosed our findings to affected CDN providers and have received constructive feedback.

articleTitle: Using Computer-Aided Models to Support Ski Resorts Planning from the Perspective of Sport-Tourism Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Recently, ski resorts has achieved widespread attention following the flourish of winter sports and world-wide events. Towards economical and sustainable development, it is necessary to explore ski resorts' transformation from traditional winter season operation to innovative year-round operation. This article conducts a comprehensive analysis of ski resorts in north-east and north parts of China. It tries to explore the characteristics, challenges and development potentials of these selected ski resorts within the perspective of sport-tourism integration. Methods of comparison analysis, case study and three-dimensional modelling are employed. The conclusion indicates that (1) services and business of ski resorts could be diversified with the some symbols of ice and snow industry. (2) suitable spatial planning and design schemes are necessary basing on natural resource and conditions. (3) Traditional skiing project in ski resorts needs to be expanded into a wide variety of outdoor sports according to different festivals, events and season series.

articleTitle: Towards Better Top-K Recommendation with Attention-Aware Collaborative Matrix Factorization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: One of the key issues in top-K recommendation systems is how to evaluate the relevance of candidate items effectively. Conventional recommendation systems typically employ collaborative filtering techniques to compute the similarity or relevance between items. Though great success is being made by matrix factorization, as one of those most representative techniques, is claimed to be less effective in capturing the inherent sequential information between the interactions of user and item. Meanwhile, the self-attention mechanism specializes in handling sequence data, which makes it a wise option to compensate for such information loss in the above case. Until now, there has been little focus on combining these two techniques for the top- K recommendation systems. To this end, this paper introduces a hybrid deep model called Attention-Aware Collaborative Matrix Factorization (AA-CMF), which integrates the self-attention mechanism, neural networks, and matrix factorization to provide a better recommendation. By jointly learning user and item features in a unified framework, it enables a refined prediction of user preferences. More importantly, the model has the strong capability to capture the sequential relationship and dependencies between users and items, as well as among different items, thus boosting the recommendation performance. Extensive experiments were carried out on three real-world datasets, and the findings clearly indicate that AA-CMF surpasses state-of-the-art methods across multiple evaluation metrics. The empirical results also confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed model on sparse datasets.

articleTitle: Proof of Stake and Activity: Rewarding On-Chain Activity Through Consensus
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: We are introducing a novel consensus protocol for blockchain, called Proof of Stake and Activity (PoSA) which can augment the traditional Proof of Stake methods by integrating a unique Proof of Activity system. PoSA offers a compelling economic model that promotes decentralization by rewarding validators based on their staked capital and also the business value they contribute to the chain. This protocol has been implemented already into a fully-fledged blockchain platform called Bahamut (www.bahamut.io) which is designed specifically for iGaming and other markets, is actively operating in Emirati and boasts hundreds of thousands of active users.

articleTitle: Contrastive Regularized Graph Autoencoder for Node Clustering with Pair-Wise Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Node clustering aims to discover communities in graph data. Recent node clustering methods managed to sufficiently explore the graph information, but they still not perform on par with classification methods, due to the lack of label guidance. Despite definitely an unsupervised task clustering is, there are ubiquitous real-world scenarios where not labels but constraints are easily accessible. These constraints typically include pairs of nodes that are closely related and should be assigned to the same community. Such constraints can also be used as supervision and help with the clustering. However, previous clustering methods for attributed graph data can barely utilize such supervision. These facts lead us here to propose an autoencoder-based method for constrained node clustering in attributed graphs. We exploit the graph information with a graph auto encoder, which can learn sufficient node embedding from the graph data. To take advantage of the available constraints, a contrastive loss-based regularization term is further designed to model the pair-wise relationship and manipulate the latent embedding. Experimental results on benchmark graph datasets show that our algorithm significantly lifts the graph clustering performance with the help of the provided pairwise constraints information.

articleTitle: Enhancing Pneumonia Diagnosis Using a Ensemble Transformer-Based Attention Network for Chest X-Ray Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: The intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and medical imaging has significantly advanced the diagnosis of pneumonia, a leading cause of mortality worldwide. This paper presents a novel ensemble transformer-based attention network architecture that enhances the detection of pneumonia in chest X-ray images, leveraging the comprehensive Chest X-ray14 dataset. Our model integrates the strengths of GoogleNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet, refined by a sophisticated attention mechanism, yielding a robust framework for medical diagnosis. In a comparative study against established models such as GoogleNet, ResNet50, DenseNet, p-ResNet, and MobileNet, our approach demonstrated superior diagnostic performance, particularly for pneumonia, with an AVC of 91.3. The proposed model also showed exceptional capabilities in identifying other thoracic pathologies like Cardiomegaly, Edema, and Emphysema, with competitive performance in Effusion and Mass detection. These results not only set a new benchmark in the field but also suggest the transformative potential of AI-enhanced diagnostic systems for timely and accurate pneumonia detection, paving the way for their integration into clinical workflows and the advancement of precision medicine.

articleTitle: Applying “Node-Place-Value (NPV)” Model on the Renewal of Suburban Areas Along Rail Transit Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: As an important support for the development of urban-rural tourism interaction, the villages along the rail transit lines are gradually linking with the tourism core areas of cities. In order to further explore the mechanism of rail transit construction in enhancing the efficiency of the villages, the Node-Place model is integrated into the rural development characteristics, introducing cultural tourism values as the third dimension, and proposing the Node- Place-Value model to evaluate the accessibility of the villages and their coupling degree with land, industry, and other factors from a three-dimensional quantitative perspective. Taking Liuliqu Village, Beijing, as a study case, the evaluation indicators and weighting results are calculated to analyze the status of the station. It is found that Liuliqu Village station area is in a status of “imbalance” so that based on the analysis of the model results. Strategies to improve the quality of public space of Liuliqu are proposed from the dimensions of node, place, and cultural tourism values. Additionally, this article indicates that railway construction has a significant impact on the renewal of traditional villages, enhancing the functional capacity of rural station areas. Improvements are urgently needed in terms of transportation infrastructure and the development of cultural tourism value.

articleTitle: A Technique for Ensured Cross Chain IBC Transactions Using TPM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Cross chain contact across several blockchains becomes increasingly significant in importance with the increased use of blockchain technology. However, security cannot be assured when producing equivalent outputs through cross-chain transmission because it is simple to launch an assault, and without security measures; it is simple to cause the transmission material to be stolen. This article combines TPM, IBC, and associates encryption and decryption techniques for protection to overcome this issue. We have establishes the viability and efficacy of the suggested method through testing and performance analyses. The experimental findings show that our approach can successfully preserve privacy and guarantee the security of data transfer.

articleTitle: Research on Buffer Overflow Vulnerability Mining Method Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: Buffer overflow vulnerability is the most widespread and destructive vulnerability in software security, the existing mining methods need to manually analyze the program code based on preset rules, the workload is large and the efficiency and accuracy are relatively low. To mine buffer overflow vulnerabilities more efficiently and accurately, in this paper, we design a model for buffer overflow vulnerability mining at the level of program source code using deep learning techniques. According to the common sensitive functions that are prone to buffer overflow vulnerabilities, we obtain the potentially vulnerable code from the source code to generate a vulnerability code block, and then based on the parsed code attribute maps analyze the buffer overflow sensitive function call mode, for different function call modes, different slicing methods will be used to construct the vulnerability code block into code slices. The code slices are mapped into numeric vectors by the Word2vec word vector model. The buffer overflow vulnerability mining model for the Bi-GRU-Attn network was optimized using the Particle Swarm Algorithm, Keepy Method, and Attention Mechanism and the model was trained and tested using the CWE-119 (Buffer Errors) dataset from the benchmark dataset SARD. In this paper, we have conducted comparative experiments in five aspects: precision rate, recall rate, false alarm rate, F1 value, and UC value, and the results show that the proposed model can mine buffer overflow vulnerabilities effectively and has better results in improving precision rate and reducing false alarm rate.

articleTitle: Secure and Efficient Certificateless Linearly Homomorphic Signature Scheme for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: With the development of network technology, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have attracted widespread attention. However, in wireless sensor networks, sensor nodes are often distributed in harsh physical environments and communicate wirelessly with each other, so the data are vulnerable to tampering and forgery by third parties. Digital signature can be used as a security mechanism to solve the above problem. But the traditional digital signature technology needs to sign every message, which is not appropriate for sensor nodes limited by power and communication bandwidth. According to the practical application requirements of WSNs, this paper proposes a certificateless linearly homomorphic signature scheme for data transmission and authentication. The scheme can be used to ensure the authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation of data in WSNs. Furthermore, the security of the constructed scheme is proved in the random oracle model. The performance analysis shows that the scheme has certain advantages in overall performance.

articleTitle: A Secure, Flexible and Decentralized Data Sharing Scheme for InterPlanetary File System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
abstract: The InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) has revolutionized data storage and retrieval. However, its official standard and implementation do not provide supports for secure data sharing which is an essential service of remote data storage systems. Although there are some attempts to address the secure data sharing problem for IPFS, a suitable scheme for open and decentralized system is still lacking. This paper grasps three essential goals including data confidentiality, sharing flexibility and decentralization of data sharing for IPFS. It proposes a secure, flexible and decentralized data sharing scheme, involving a file storing smart contract and a re-capsule smart contract to support flexible data sharing in a purely decentralized manner. A prototype is realized and a set of experiments are done in the Polygon test network Mumbai. The results show that the proposed scheme achieves the three goals with affordable costs.
